title: Wolfult
text: So, we came back from Wolf’s house, indeed. Father was giving Rival and Rafumi a report on what had happened. However, that report ended up triggering yet another development.
“Hey. Spear Hero.”
“What is it, I say?”
I’d returned to the village and was tending to the Filolial-samas when Rafumi called out to me.
“With our current materials and technology, it would take too much effort to make on my own. There’s something I want to make, so help me.”
“No thank you, I say. What exactly are you trying to make me help with?”
Rafumi was giving me some strange order again.
“Don’t say that. I haven’t had much fun lately, have I? I’d like to do something a little entertaining.”
“I wouldn’t know anything about that. You’re surely off somewhere having fun teasing someone already, indeed.”
Rafumi was absolutely, without a doubt, off somewhere toying with someone for entertainment. I’d rather die than help with something like that.
“Oh? Are you defying my orders? Hm? Do you want to see it again?”
“Guh…”
That Rafumi! Is she planning to do the face-only-Filo-tan of Rafumi thing again!? I could tell without a doubt that was the threat she was making.
“In that case, this time I really will go out of my way to make sure Gaelion doesn’t take Shield Hero’s virginity, just as he wishes.”
“You’re not allowed either, indeed.”
Rival being forbidden was an absolute given, but Rafumi taking Father’s virginity was also something I absolutely could not allow. As we argued back and forth, Rival came drifting over slowly.
“Knew it, nano. You’re roping him in again, nano.”
“Hmph. Sharp-eyed as ever. What’s wrong with something this minor?”
“Nano, it’s not worth making a fuss over, nano, I won’t deny that. Well, Rival can tell you’re trying to sneak in a little something extra, nano.”
“That’s right. I got curious what would happen if I added a small extra to the event I so considerately sat out of. Fufu… stirring up something that’s neatly settled… might be fun, don’t you think?”
“You really do chase after fleeting fun too much, nano.”
Rival and Rafumi were having some odd conversation between just the two of them. Do whatever you want, I say.
“Get lost already, the Filolial-samas’ moods sour if you two stick around here, indeed.”
Mostly because of Rival.
“Getting back to the topic—calling it fleeting is a bit much. I was giving serious thought to whether the Raph-species should continue to exist in this world’s future.”
Listen to me when I’m talking, Rafumi and Rival, I say.
“Are you making another one? You should just have the Hammer make it, indeed.”
I’d made one before as a gift for Father, but in this loop he hadn’t shown much interest in it. Serves Rafumi right, I say.
“Even if I wanted to make one, I lack the necessary unlock skills. To begin with, I’m only a proxy owner, so I can’t draw out its full performance.”
“Nano, and in this loop we’re missing the key part to begin with, so we can’t make the original Raph-chan that Naofumi was so fond of, nano.”

“Well, that’s true. Still, considering long-term stability, wouldn’t it be nice to have something similar around? As a spirit, my judgment is that this loop is likely to earn a rather interesting evaluation.”
“Nano, having to worry about how the spirits will evaluate things too seems like a lot, nano.”

“It’s about seeking a lasting way to be of use to both the Filo the Spear Hero wishes for and to Shield Hero’s strength. I’d think twice about refusing to cooperate, wouldn’t you? You know full well what it is I desire.”
Haa… Rival let out a sigh.
“You really are something, nano.”
“Well then, let’s go.”
“Yes, yes, nano.”

So saying, Rafumi and Rival wandered off somewhere for a while, and then came back again. Rafumi produced something… some sort of crystal, similar to the ones Rival used to make when creating Raph-species.
“This time’s material is this.”
Looking at the crystal… I could faintly make out something like a Phantom Wolf’s face floating and wavering inside it.

“Think of it as a guardian spirit. Thanks to the power of Claw’s Seven Star Weapon, a remnant lingered on in the shadows, and I had Gaelion carefully and quietly peel it off without being noticed, then fixed it in place.”
“What in the world is it, I say?”
“Nano, this is just speculation, but maybe some distant relative that turned into a ghost and went on a rampage, nano? Rifana—ahem, ahem—she’s alive, but part of her ancestry might overlap, nano.”
Something about how tenacity even after becoming a ghost was apparently a shared trait—Rival was saying things that only she and Rafumi seemed to understand.
“That part is certainly significant. But the current state also involves Claw, I’d wager. Call it a consideration. In a sense, it’s being treated similarly to Hakuko’s daughter.”
“Nano, I suppose that’s fitting for a spirit, in a way. Well, compared to that, let’s just make it easier to move around, nano.”
“Fufufu… using this material, I’m sure even Azott and the others will react in interesting ways.”
“Nano, sneaky of you to tie that in too, nano.”
There stood Rafumi, laughing fufufu.
“There, Spear Hero. We’ve gathered the materials, so help out, nano.”
“So why exactly do I have to help, I say?”
“Because otherwise Rafumi gets to be a pain, nano.”
“Come now, just comply obediently. Or else, who knows what I might do, hmmmmm?”
Ngh… this was seriously a pain.
“Just this once, I say.”
“Whether I’ll honor that agreement, who can say? Well, in this loop, I won’t ask you for any more life creation beyond this.”
With no other choice, I ended up helping make something Raph-species-like.
“This time’s material is this.”
What was brought out was… some kind of fur, apparently.
“For the body, this, and this, and this fur from Azott the inult, plus this thing—a gene sample taken from an inult on Cal Mira Island.”

All of it was fur. Judging by the smell, it was Wolf, Keel, and Ren. All dogs, I say. The last item was some sort of tool. What on earth were they making? Whatever came out of this was surely going to be a dog. Thinking that, I used my alchemy skill alongside Rival and Rafumi, going through almost the same process as when making Raph-species. What floated in the culture tank was… a creature with more fur than Keel, Ren, or an inult would normally have, with a different sort of dog-like quality, the kind of thing Luna would probably love. Its coloring was mixed with silver. …It looked like a small Wolf. Wolf plus inult… something like “Wolfult,” I say. In appearance, a dog; on the inside, Raph-species.
“Now, all that’s left is to insert this crystallized key component, and—done!”
And so, the creature we’d made was complete.
“Now then, let’s go show off the finished product to Shield Hero, shall we?”
“Will this make Father give me more side dishes, I say?”
Somehow, I doubted it would go that smoothly.
“Nano, probably nothing’ll change, but Gaelion will explain things to some extent, so just come along, nano.”
Ugh… my standing here really was low, I say. Thinking such thoughts, we headed off toward Father.
“Huh? Motoyasu-kun and… what an unusual combination to show up together. What’s going on?”
We’d come to find Father, who was helping with reconstruction work and keeping an eye on things in Big Sister’s village. There, we found Big Sister, Older Sister, and Big Sister’s friend.
“Rafumi ordered me around and I ended up making a creature, indeed. I’d like you to take a look, I say.”
“Eh? Is it safe, nano?”
“It’s safe, nano! The production process is almost identical to the creature Naofumi got so absorbed in during another loop, nano.”
“Ohh?”
“Eh…”
“Wow, I wonder what’s going to come out?”
Big Sister and the others were each looking at us.
“Introducing it here is quite the twist of fate, nano.”
For some reason, Rival was looking at Big Sister’s friend.
“Well then, allow us to introduce it. There, make your debut.”
“Ruff!”
It peeked out, taking one step forward from behind Rafumi, raising a paw as if to say “Nice to meet you!” and showing itself off.
